When Claude calls task_close on a task for the person with how claude_did, person_did or not_needed and the input that kind needs, the task closes and the board shows who closed it, how, and the note or the quoted words, with a reopen button.
When Claude calls task_close with claude_did on an answer or decide task, with words in said that no prompt of the person since the task was asked holds, or with any other wrong input, the call is refused by name and the task stays open.
When a person prompt arrives while tasks for the person are open, it carries one line that lists at most 5 open tasks and asks Claude to close one with task_close when the prompt says it was done.

## Context

Owner, 2026-11-19, his words: "the tasks on the board should be closable by agents too, not only humans, as many of them from experience can also be done by an agent, or a human instead of opening the board and checking the tasks just writes what he has done in the chat. this needs a bit of thought, and honestly it is not that clearly visible and the text is cut off of nthe buttons (or was cut in last version). for sure needs re-eingineering and improvement as well."

Today a task that Claude assigns to the person (task_assign, kinds do, answer and decide) closes only by a press on the board. Intended outcome: Claude can close such a task through a board tool when the person says in the chat that it is done, or when Claude did it, and the board shows who closed it; the tasks for the person are easier to see, and no button text is cut.

Design decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-19 12:14 UTC (dev-j6oqo), all 7 recommended answers: Q1 a new tool task_close; Q2 one withdraw path (not_needed; task_update removed on a person task is refused and names task_close); Q3 said is checked literally against the person's prompts kept in memory (at most 20); Q4 the per-prompt line, at most 5 tasks, token cost measured for the release message; Q5 reopen while the row is listed, not an undo; Q6 band B; Q7 a decide close needs the option text inside the quote. Mocks go into docs/mocks.md as section 20.

## Confirmation Plan

claude plugin test mods/handily-board with new tests per criterion; a live tmux check in Code Mode where the person says in the chat that a task is done and Claude closes it with the quote, and one where the quote does not match and the close is refused; screens at 120, 80 and 40 columns.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Request to the basicly project (owner of core/output-styles/tired-engineer/style.yaml)

The person asked on 2026-10-09 to adapt the tired-engineer style to the handily terminal mods (installed at user scope, so they draw every repository's transcript). Not delivered: the basicly session had ended. Hand it to the next basicly session.

Proposed additions under Shape:
1. A table has at most 3 columns; a cell holds at most about 40 characters; longer text goes in a list under the table.
2. A table cell holds plain words or one code span, no bold, no link, so a copy as plain text pastes clean into an email or a chat.
3. Put the verdict, the bad news and any question in the first 30 lines; a terminal view folds the rest (handily-cvqn7).
4. Give each command that the reader runs its own fenced block, so a copy button copies exactly that command.
5. No emoji and no box-drawing characters in text; they draw 2 columns wide in many terminals. The 1-column cell marks ✓ ✗ → stay.

## Evidence

- Screenshots 2026-10-09: a 4-column table with long cells drew as about 45 lines of blocks.

payload.text: Tested 2026-10-09 in handily (A/B, same prompt, 2 runs each, Claude Code 2.1.295, insert after the 'Symbols in tables only' paragraph of the tired-engineer style): cells over 40 characters 8 and 16 of 48 -> 1 and 2 of 48; longest cell 58 and 103 -> 43 and 45; longest table line 113 and 194 -> 90 and 100; columns, verdict line, bold-free cells and command blocks unchanged. Exact text: **Narrow tables.** A table has at most 3 columns, and a cell holds at most about 40 characters. Put longer text in a list under the table. A cell holds plain words or one code span, with no bold and no link, so that the table copies clean into an email or a chat. **The first 30 lines carry the answer.** Put the verdict, the bad news and any question in the first 30 lines. A terminal view can fold the rest. **One command per block.** Give each command that the reader runs its own fenced block, so that a copy button copies exactly that command. **One-column characters.** Use no emoji and no box-drawing characters in text. Many terminals draw them 2 columns wide, and they break the alignment. The person asks basicly to ship it as a patch release.

## Context

The test 'a draw with 30 agents of 20 tasks reads the state 5 times' failed in 4 of about 12 runs on 2026-10-28, while the machine was loaded. An instrumented run showed 4 extra get and set pairs on the agents key during the mount, which cause a second draw. The cause is unknown. The intended outcome is a test that passes on every run, or a fixed cause.

## Scope

- mods/handily-board

payload.description:
## Context
Found on 2026-11-12. .claude-plugin/marketplace.json gives each mod a relative source such as ./mods/handily-board, so Claude Code installs each mod from its folder on the default branch, main. A release tag such as handily-reply-view--v0.24.0 only makes a GitHub release with notes. So every merge into main reaches a fresh install at once, under the old version label, and a user with that version cached does not refetch. The owner keeps release, deploy and delete; that protects only the tag, not what users get. Example: handily-36bsx.9.1 merged into main with a fold defect behind the default-on sideBySide setting, and a fresh install of reply-view got it labelled 0.24.0.

## Options
(a) Each marketplace entry points at the release tag of its mod. Cost: the generator writes the tag ref with the version at each release; it must first be checked against the current Claude Code plugin marketplace docs that a plugin source can name a git ref together with a subfolder of the repository. Main stays the working branch.
(b) Lanes merge into an integration branch, and main moves only at a release. Cost: a second long-lived branch to keep in sync, CI and the ledger commits on both, and the lane and worktree tooling based on main changes.
(c) Keep main, and treat each merge into main as a release that needs the owner. Cost: no new mechanism, but every lane waits for the owner, which slows the work while the owner is away.

Recommendation: (a), if the marketplace supports a ref with a subfolder, because it ties what users get to the tag the owner approved and leaves the lane flow alone. If it does not, (b). Until the owner decides, the orchestrator rule holds: a lane merges into main only when main is safe to install at that commit.
payload.title: marketplace: every merge into main reaches a fresh install with no release

payload.text: [fact 2026-11-12] Option (a) is supported by the docs. A git-subdir plugin source takes url (a git URL or the owner/repo shorthand), path (the subfolder, fetched with a sparse checkout), ref (a branch or tag, default the default branch) and sha (a full commit, checked out when both are set). Sources read 2026-11-12, no page date shown: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Create a marketplace) and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/marketplace-reference.md (Plugin sources, git-subdir plugin source). Example entry: name handily-board, source {source git-subdir, url niksavis/handily, path mods/handily-board, ref handily-board--v0.22.0}; claude plugin validate --strict passed on Claude Code 2.1.322, and the same entry without path failed with plugins.0.source Invalid input. Caution: validate also passed a github source with a path field it does not have, so a pass does not prove that ref and path are used. Not established: that an install checks out the folder at that tag, and that a ref with -- fetches; settle it by installing in an isolated config directory and reading the cached version. git ls-remote shows the tag at adf66960efeaddd5c48afa97dc9f93637cce3001.

[install test 2026-11-12] Decided by the orchestrator and run on Claude Code 2.1.322 with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to two fresh folders in the session scratchpad; the owner's own plugin configuration lists no probe entry afterwards. 1 git-subdir with url niksavis/handily, path mods/handily-board, ref handily-board--v0.22.0: marketplace add and plugin install exit 0; installed_plugins.json shows version 0.22.0 and gitCommitSha 67a9b1db28bd359dffe2fa63b6e6e4fe1f5049e5, which is the commit of the tag (git rev-parse handily-board--v0.22.0^{commit}); the cached hooks hold none of retry.ts, pace.ts or limit-warn.ts that main has, so the install took the tag content, not main. The ref with -- fetched. 2 the same entry with sha 67a9b1db28bd359dffe2fa63b6e6e4fe1f5049e5 in place of ref: exit 0, same version and commit, same absence of the main-only files. Both warned: dependency handily-workitems was not installed because the probe marketplace does not list it, so a git-subdir marketplace must list every mod, each at its own tag. Option (a) works.

[decision 2026-11-12] Decided by the orchestrator: option (a). Build: the marketplace lists every mod as a git-subdir source at its latest release tag, with ref (the tag) and sha (the tag commit); the generator writes them at each release, and the report must say whether in the release commit or right after the tag exists. Mistake proofing: a check fails on a tag that does not exist, a sha that is not the tag commit, or a mod on main with no entry; dependencies resolve inside the marketplace each at its own tag, with a test for the dependency was not installed warning. Order: after C3 and C2 of handily-36bsx.9; decompose first and send the children; priority 1 after the side by side defect is off main. The commit that changes the live marketplace file is a release step and waits for the owner; the request names what users get before and after, and that unreleased work on main is not installed until its release.

[decomposition proposed 2026-11-12] Sent to the orchestrator. Pin timing: right after the tag exists, in its own commit, because the sha is the release commit and a commit cannot hold its own hash; plain npm run marketplace keeps every pin, and --pin NAME moves one. Children: 1 scripts: the generator pins a mod at its release tag (ref and the peeled tag commit; refuses a missing tag; scope scripts/mods.mjs and its test). 2 scripts: validate refuses an entry that does not install its tag (missing tag, wrong sha, a tagged mod with no entry, a dependency the marketplace does not list; an untagged mod gets a note). 3 scripts: the install gate installs every mod at its tag in a clean profile (network fetches from GitHub). 4 marketplace: a fresh install gets each mod at its release tag, the owner release step (marketplace.json, fetch-depth 0 and tags in both workflows, docs, the relative branch removed). Order: 1, then 2 and 3, then 4. Breaks at the switch: install-gate.mjs line 151 reads a path source; mods.mjs lines 297 and 345 write and require relative sources; both workflows check out shallow with no tags; release.yml line 93 runs claude plugin tag. Missing fact: whether claude plugin tag accepts a git-subdir entry whose version differs from plugin.json, or has no version; the decomposer probe of claude plugin tag --dry-run was denied by the permission check and was not retried.

[decision 2026-11-12] Decided by the orchestrator: the cut into 4 children and the order 1, then 2 and 3, then 4 are approved; the pin goes in its own commit right after the tag exists. Child 1 starts now beside C3. Child 3 may fetch from the owner public repository into a clean profile in a scratch folder, on this machine and in CI, never the owner real plugin configuration, and installs the whole tagged set at once. Child 4 stays the owner step as a whole, with the two workflow edits, and its request includes one live session check with the full tagged set loaded. The open fact on claude plugin tag: first a researcher reads the docs; second, design so the question does not arise.

The head is never cut. Design B, a list of up to 2 titles under the head, not recommended. A refused batch keeps the generic error row. Row type: kind addedMany with ids, before and titles; the test at board.test.ts:3518 flips. Open questions: Q1 design A (taste); Q2 two ids as 3, 4 and three or more as 3-7, follows /board plan in 8.11j; Q3 no board row of its own for a refused batch (taste).

[decision 2026-11-12] Decided by the orchestrator: approved with design A. Q2 two ids as 3, 4 and three or more as a range, from 8.11j; a range only when the ids are consecutive, else the ids are listed and cut with +N when they do not fit, with a test. Q1 and Q3 are taste, decided for now.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Found by the handily-cli304 lane on 2026-11-18: the tasks Pane render still arms $.clock.after(0, () => clearBandEnds($, 'isFailureSeen')) in mods/handily-board/hooks/register.tsx near the hasStripFailure check. On Claude Code 2.1.327 a state write from a timer that fires while the render is pending is denied (same host check as handily-cli304). Moving it changes when the failed band row clears, which the test a failed row leaves the band once the board opens from the band and the this session tab shows pins.

Intended outcome: the tasks pane draw writes no state. It notes in memory which failed agent rows it drew, so the band hides those rows at once. A hook that may write state (a command, a prompt, a turn end, a pane close) then marks exactly those agents as seen. An agent that fails after the draw keeps its row in the band.

## Confirmation Plan

claude plugin test mods/handily-board, with the failed row tests of board.test.ts extended to fail on a state write from the tasks pane draw. payload.acceptance_criteria:
When the Session section draws in a frame (terminal, body 41 or more), its title ends with the waits, if any, and then ▶ working while a main turn runs or ○ idle after it.
When the board knows the context window, the first Session row shows the tokens over the window as 663k/1.0M after the percent.
When a main-loop request reports, the model row counts the main-loop requests as N req and shows the latest time to first token as ttft 1.2s. Before any request it shows req — and no ttft.
When the body is 56 columns or wider, each limit shows resets 2h after its percent. Narrower, the reset times stay in the details.
When a permission check settles, the gate row shows the total after gate. A counts row shows allowed, asked and denied, with denied in error and never cut. Three plain Buttons with hotkeys f, s and o name the file, shell and other counts.
When the person presses f, s or o, or the Button, the last 5 checks of that family show with the verdict word first and the credentials masked. Pressing the same key again hides them.
When the agents that are not folded fit side by side as cards of at least 18 columns (2 at body 41, 4 at body 89, never more than 5), each draws as a card with a title Button, the state word, the wait or failure line, the task, the type, the ctx and out tokens, the steps and a clock that ticks each second while the tab shows.
When cards do not fit, a body of 80 or more draws the lanes and a narrower body draws rows. Inline and desktop always draw rows.
When the person presses a digit 1 to 5 while the board has the keyboard, that agent opens, and the same digit closes it. A sixth agent has no digit.
When a prompt, a spawn, a completion, an edit, an error or a denial happens, the Log shows it newest first as time, who and what, with credentials masked. It keeps the last 100 events and shows 5 at body 41, 3 at body 30 and none inline.
When an agent card is open or its transcript is in view, the Log shows only that agent's events under a dim filter line.
When the palette setting of the handily bundle is catppuccin-mocha and the theme is dark, the frames and the gauge fill draw the hex values of mocks 14.4 and every state keeps its theme key. When the theme is light or cannot be read, theme keys draw.
When /handily palette runs, it replies with the stored value, the theme, and one line for each role with its theme key and hex. Each mod keeps a byte-identical hooks/palette.ts checked by scripts/copies.mjs.
When /board stats runs, it prints the requests, the ttft, the tokens over the window, the resets and the verdicts as words. When /board log runs, it prints the kept log.

When the width tests draw ages 4m, 18s and now at the right edge, in both glyph sets, the last character of each sits in the last body column.

When the reference tests run slower than their reference times, npm test shall scale the time share by the median ratio.

payload.description:
## Context

npm test refuses a test that takes more than a third of its time limit. The share is tuned for one reference developer machine. On a machine 3.5 to 6 times slower, all tests pass but 3 to 5 different tests per run exceed the share, so no commit that touches mods or scripts passes the pre-commit hook. A machine slower than CI cannot predict a CI timeout with the share, and there the time limit alone is the gate, as on CI.
payload.title: Scale the test time share to the speed of the machine

- When a successful Bash output has no bashEditDiff field, simple-view shall draw the dim line File changes were not tracked for this call under the row.
- When a successful Bash output has no bashEditDiff field, /simple show N shall not print File diff: none.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the engine sends no bashEditDiff for a Bash call, I want the row and /simple show N to say that file changes were not tracked, so a write never reads as no change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Claude Code 2.1.294, bashEditDiffEnabled not set, auto mode.
2. Bash: printf 'x\n' >> notes.txt && sed -i 's/b/B/' new.txt
3. The row draws no result block. /simple show N prints File diff: none.

## Evidence

- Live tmux run 2026-10-08. The engine full view also shows no diff, so the engine did not track the call.
- The 2.1.294 binary has the setting bashEditDiffEnabled (Whether the Bash tool shows a diff of the files a Bash command changed) and the env CLAUDE_CODE_BASH_EDIT_DIFF.
- mods/simple-view/hooks/output.ts bashChanges returns isTracked true with zero files when the field is undefined.

## Scope

- mods/simple-view/hooks/output.ts
- mods/simple-view/hooks/detail.ts
- mods/simple-view/simple-view.test.ts
- mods/simple-view/README.md
- docs/design.md
payload.title: simple-view: a Bash call without bashEditDiff reads as not tracked, not as no changes

payload.value:
## Trigger

When the engine sends no bashEditDiff for a Bash call, I want simple-view to say that file changes were not tracked, so I can trust that a call without an Updated line changed no file.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Claude Code 2.1.294, bashEditDiffEnabled not set, auto mode.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Owner, 2026-11-18, his words: "there is an annoying bug or behavior in terminal, the model writes the response text 1st, and then handily formats it, because the text is streaming in real time. is it not better that handily captures that text stream 1st and show ist won animation in terminal, and its own output, and not letting the model write and then applying the layout style. it is making things hard to read, making thext change shape and size and just wasting time and ruining focus."

Today (README.md:102): while a reply streams, Claude Code draws it, and reply-view draws it once complete, so the look changes at the end.

Plan, decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-18: a turn.step hook holds back the text chunks of each text block; the Spinner line shows reply-view progress; the block is released whole and drawn formatted. Esc releases held text at once; a held block is released after at most a few seconds even if not complete, so a long block never looks hung (measure and name the bound). Default on, with a setting for live streaming.

payload.value:
- When a reply streams on the terminal, no raw text of a text block shows before reply-view draws it; the block appears in its final layout, and the spinner line shows reply-view progress meanwhile.
- When the person presses Esc during a held block, the held text shows at once and is kept in the transcript.
- When a text block streams longer than the named bound, the held text is released and drawn so far, so the reply never looks hung.
- When the person sets the live streaming setting, replies stream as Claude Code draws them today.

When the installed basicly is 0.21.1 or later, I want workitems to read basicly items without a repo approval where that is safe, so I can see the items of a repo without a question that no longer guards anything.

payload.value:
- A folded tool row has a more button that opens at most 20 lines of the output under the row, then an all N lines button, and a less button that folds it again.

- A reply longer than 12 lines draws its first lines and a count of the hidden lines with a more button that shows the whole reply and a copy button that copies the whole reply as markdown.
- A markdown table in a reply draws without box lines, with aligned columns and a bold header, and as one block per row when the columns do not fit the width.
- A table has a copy button that copies it as markdown and a copy as text button that copies label and value lines.
- A fenced block draws a title line from its tag and a copy button that copies the block content only.
- A toggle command turns the reply view off and on for the session, and while it is off the engine draws replies unchanged.
- The handily bundle lists the new mod, the READMEs describe the folds and the copy buttons, and npm run check passes.

payload.description:
## Context

A pane parses test runner output from Bash calls: vitest, jest, node --test, pytest, cargo and go. It lists each failure with its assertion diff and keeps a run history. The status line shows tests 3 of 4 passed. The owning mod is open: a new mod or simple-view.

Reference: redgreen (MIT). Source: survey of github.com/karanb192/awesome-claude-code-mods and its reference mods on 2026-10-28. Clones were read only. handily copies no code and adds no dependency.
payload.title: A tests pane with failures by name and a status line count

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
When a Bash call runs vitest, jest, node --test or pytest and a test fails, the tests tab lists each failed test by name, with its file, its line and its assertion diff.
The runner is found from the output format, so npm test that runs vitest counts as vitest.
When the output has no known runner format, the tab, the status line and the toasts do not change.
When the last run has a failure, the status line reads tests: 1 failed · 3 of 4 passed. With statusLine set to off, the mod sets no status line.
When the output was cut, the run went to the background or the call was interrupted, the tab says so in words and never shows a pass.
/tests opens the tab, /tests close closes it, /tests list prints the last run as text and /tests clear empties it.
The bundle handily lists handily-tests, and /handily shows its version and state.
Each parser is tested with hand-written output fixtures of its runner, kept in the repo. No runner is added as a dependency.

payload.title: board: a clear mark that a session is idle, working or waiting on background work

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Owner request of 2026-11-16, in his words: "i need a good visual indicator if a session is idle, working, waiting as sometimes it is not clear. for example when a session is waiting on a CI build. in the terminal it looks as nothing is happening."

Today the board Session card says idle or working, and Claude Code shows its own spinner only while a turn runs. When a turn ends with background work in flight (a background shell such as gh run watch, a Monitor, a background subagent, a scheduled wakeup), the terminal shows a quiet prompt, so a waiting session looks the same as an idle one. The classic Stop hook input names this case: background_tasks lists in-flight work and session_crons lists scheduled wakeups; handily registers no classic hook, so the function-hook signal is still to be established.

payload.text: [probe 2026-11-16] Claude Code 2.1.325 in tmux with a scratch mod that registers a classic.Stop function hook and turn.start, under the organisation security plugin. Claude started sleep 90 with run_in_background. The Stop at the end of that turn reported tasks=[{id, type shell, status running, description Wait 90 seconds in the background, command sleep 90}] crons=[]. When the shell ended, the engine woke a turn (Background command completed, then turn.start main), and the Stop of that turn reported tasks=[] crons=[]. So the function-hook Stop input reaches a mod and separates waiting on background work from idle for the main session. Owner decisions of 2026-11-16 (answer go): the probe first; the waiting colour is the theme key suggestion; the status line carries waiting under attention. Design: mocks A to F from the designer agent, recommended A plus C plus D plus E.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a main session turn ends and the Stop input lists background work or session crons, the board shows waiting with the mark, the age and the first item, on the band, the status line under attention and the Session card head, on terminal and desktop.
- When the next turn starts or a Stop input lists no background work and no crons, the board clears waiting and shows working or idle.
- When the Stop input has no background list, the board shows no turn and never idle.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a session runs tools, I want each tool call drawn as one readable row with what it does and how it ended, so I can follow the work without reading raw commands, JSON and output walls.

## Decisions (user, 2026-10-08)

- Scope: every tool, not Bash only.
- Raw view: the ctrl+o transcript shows the raw rows, if a probe confirms the engine allows it; a slash command toggles the mod for the session, like /quiet-items.
- Done row: the description, the exit code, the line count and the time; on a failure, the first error line.

## Open questions

- The ToolUse props carry no start time, so the elapsed time may need the mod's own clock.
- Whether a ToolUse rewrite yields to the raw row in the ctrl+o transcript.
- The engine's file-change diff (Updated <file> (+N -0)) is not a RenderComponent, so the mod may not reach it.
- quiet-items keeps the rows of tracker writes; tool-rows must defer to it.

## Scope

- mods/tool-rows/
- .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
- docs/design.md
- docs/mocks.md

payload.title: tool-rows: a new mod that draws each tool call as one readable row

payload.text: Usage 2026-10-08, measured over 94 local session transcripts (top-level only, no subagents): 13356 tool calls; Bash 11744 (88 percent), Edit 327, SendMessage 268, Write 239, Read 194, Agent 130, WebFetch 114. Programs inside Bash segments: git 6553, uv 5927, head 5253, tail 4423, grep 3958, rg 3281, python3 3187, sed 2904, cat 1793, ls 1010, gh 667, wc 640, jq 511, basicly 338, find 168, fd 11, yq 6. User priority: the tools Claude Code uses most. So tool-rows starts with Bash and reads the program inside it (git, uv, grep or rg, head or tail, sed, python3, gh, jq), then Edit, Write and Read.

Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion. Agreed: no start time in ToolUse props, so measure around next(e) with the mod clock (it includes approval waits); ToolUse has no ctrl+o signal, so the raw view is the /tool-rows toggle; Bash has no numeric exit code and the error text has no guaranteed format, so parse it when present and else show no code. Corrections from the second opinion: quiet-items ready means initialized, not that it drew a row, so tool-rows must defer by the quiet-items row state of that call, not by the ready key; the Updated file diff placement inside ToolResult needs a live probe. Biggest risk: a short row hides output or a diff with false certainty. Second opinion: build Bash first inside tool-rows, with the engine row for every case it does not cover. Live probes still open: ctrl+o, bashEditDiff placement, exit code text, the clock redraw.

Live probe 2026-10-08 (Claude Code 2.1.294, terminal): P1 the ctrl+o view is a fullscreen detailed transcript that unfolds groups and raises ToolUse and ToolResult again; the event keys are surface, component, viewport, requestId; no prop marks ctrl+o, the viewport value is not yet logged. P3 an errored Bash output is a plain string such as Error: Exit code 2 followed by the stderr lines; a successful output object has stdout, stderr, interrupted and bashEditDiff and no exit code. P2 bashEditDiff has files, moreFiles, changedFiles with hunks; no Updated block showed in the probe session, and the built-in plugin cc-plugin-diff hooks ui.render and tool.call, so it may draw the Updated block (hypothesis, needs a run without the probe). Normal view folds Bash calls into one group line, so tool-rows must also handle ToolGroup.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a Bash call finishes with no error, tool-rows shall draw one row with the description, exit 0, the stdout line count and the elapsed time, and shall draw the result row empty.
- When a Bash call errors with an output that starts with Error: Exit code N, the row shall show exit N and the first non-empty line after it.
- When the Bash input has no description, the row shall show the first command segment, cut with an ellipsis.
- While a Bash call runs, the row shall show running and the elapsed time since its tool.call.
- When the Bash output carries bashEditDiff, the row shall show the file count and the added and removed line totals.
- When quiet-items stored a row for the call, tool-rows shall pass the ToolUse and ToolResult renders on unchanged.
- When /tool-rows runs, the mod shall toggle its mode for the session and reply with the new mode; while the mode is off, every row shall draw as the engine draws it.
- If a call is interrupted, refused or a non-Bash tool, or drawing throws, tool-rows shall pass the render on unchanged.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a Bash call finishes with no error, simple-view shall draw one row with the description, the program, exit 0, the stdout line count and the elapsed time, and shall draw the result as one Updated line per changed file with its added and removed totals, or as nothing when no file changed.
- When a Bash call errors with an output that starts with Error: Exit code N, the row shall show exit N and the first non-empty line after it.
- When the Bash input has no description, the row shall show the first command segment, cut with an ellipsis.
- While a Bash call runs, the row shall show running and the elapsed time since its tool.call.
- When an Edit or Write call succeeds, simple-view shall draw one row with the file path and its added and removed line totals, without the diff body.
- When quiet-items stored a row for the call, simple-view shall pass the ToolUse and ToolResult renders on unchanged.
- When /simple runs, the mod shall toggle its mode for the session, set the quiet-items mode to the same value, and reply with the new mode; while the mode is off, every row shall draw as the engine draws it.
- When /simple show N runs, the mod shall print the full input, output and file diff of the N-th last tool call of the session; when N is out of range, it shall refuse by name and give the valid range.
- If a call is interrupted or refused, or drawing throws, simple-view shall pass the render on unchanged.

## Trigger

When a project's tracker file grows past 4 MiB, I want workitems to keep showing its items, so I can use the mods on a large or long-lived project.

## Evidence

- The person saw 'Work items unavailable: .beads/issues.jsonl is over 4 MiB.' in the task pane, 2026-10-09.
- mods/workitems/hooks/snapshot.ts:15 MAX_FILE_BYTES = 4 MiB; :104 the approval hash, :127 and :169 the reads refuse a larger file.
- Engine limits (types index.d.ts, Claude Code 2.1.295): $.fs.read rejects over 4 MiB (:3228); $.process.run keeps the first 4194304 bytes of each stream (:3510); $.process.spawn streams pieces with no stated cap (:3517-3526).

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: When .beads/issues.jsonl is over 4 MiB, workitems lists the open items through the br CLI after the person approves the run, and the pane shows them. When br is missing, the approval is refused, the output is cut at 4 MiB, or the output cannot be read, workitems shows a failure that names the cause and the fix, and shows no partial list. A file of 4 MiB or less is still read directly, as before. The approval hash still refuses a covered code file over 4 MiB by name. A test with a tracker file over 4 MiB proves each case.

payload.text: Decision 2026-10-09, the person said go with fixing this first. Option B chosen after a Codex second opinion: when .beads/issues.jsonl is over 4 MiB, list open items through the approved br CLI (br 0.3.2, list --json has no default limit). Rejected: A, streaming the file through process.spawn of cat (trust and platform cost); C, the Read tool through tool.call with offset and limit (permission prompts, file_unchanged, long-line limits unproven). Failure mode: an incomplete list makes missing items look closed under listsOpenOnly (snapshot.ts:196), so every incomplete outcome must fail by name. The CLI paths already refuse cut output (adapter.ts:66).

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When Claude runs a tool call, I want to see the mod row from the start, so I do not see raw engine output for 1 to 2 seconds before it is redrawn.

## Evidence

- Frame probe 2026-10-09 (100 ms frames, simple-view 0.4.0): the engine group line 'Running 1 shell command…' showed for about 0.7 s, then 'Bash(sleep 2; seq 1 5)' for about 0.5 s, before the mod row; a Read showed the engine 'Read' row for about 0.3 s.
- ToolUse props carry the tool name and an input that streams in; no flag marks the input complete, so the mod returns next(e) until it can read the input.
